I1.quote: Searched the full text for a gravimetric, volumetric (Sieverts) or flow measurement of gas-phase H2 uptake; none found. Hydrogen content after milling in H2 is measured only by inert gas fusion-thermal conductivity analysis and TDS.

I2.quote: Not assessed: I1 is not met.

I3.quote: Not assessed: I1 is not met.

I4.quote: Not assessed: I1 is not met.

I5.quote: We investigated the hydrogen adsorption / desorption properties of activated carbon that was prepared by mechanical milling in a hydrogen atmosphere at an ambient temperature.

notes: I1 judgment: Maxsorb activated carbon was ball-milled for 1-100 h under H2 (initial 0.8 MPa, room temperature), i.e. mechanochemical hydrogenation. The only hydrogen amounts reported come from a post-milling elemental analysis: 'The hydrogen concentration in activated carbon hydrogenated by mechanical milling was estimated by inert gas fusion-thermal conductivity method' (main, p. 2 (268), Section 3.2; Fig. 4, values to about 2.6 wt.%, net about 1.7 wt.%). Inert gas fusion-thermal conductivity (HORIBA EMGA-621W) is a thermal-extraction hydrogen analysis, analogous to the TPD/TDS also used; it is not a gravimetric, volumetric or flow uptake method, so I1 is coded not met and the code is no_conditions_stated. This is a borderline call: if an adjudicator accepts inert gas fusion as an uptake measurement, I2 would be met (activated carbon, Maxsorb), I3 would rest on 'initial pressure of 0.8 MPa' and 'room temperature' (main, p. 2 (268), Section 2.1), and I4 would be met by BET areas in Fig. 3 and text ('more than 1000 m2/g', 'about 600 m2/g after milling for 1 h', main, p. 2 (268), Section 3.1). Not a review; not retracted (record flag false, no retraction notice); no statement that the data were published before.
